classes_checked.what_was_checked: Compared outcome absence, unextracted-outcome, harm-reporting and abstract-availability claims with held abstracts, full texts and registry results.
Checked per-trial measure labels, nested study_effect fields, strand estimates and suppression of the incompatible primary pool.
Compared endpoint components, patient/event counts and reconstructed denominators with held results and table definitions.
Compared screening population decisions with held trial abstracts and registry conditions. No definite contradictory population decision established.
Checked primary-report assignments and family identities, particularly the AFFIRM-AHF quality-of-life report; accepted the supplied abstract-integrity measurements.
Compared comparator scope, reported estimates and overlap assertions with the held comparator abstract and full text.
Checked audit row identities and whether the cited evidence concerns the outcome being adjudicated.
Checked extracted metadata and numeric field provenance, including a funder identifier promoted into an outcome-value slot.

findings.title: CONFIRM-HF person-time rates become participant denominators

claim.quote: 10 of ~132 (FCM) vs 25 of ~129 (placebo) with >=1 HF hospitalisation

evidence.quote: Incidence/100 patient-years at risk are computed using the number of subjects with the end-point/event adjusted on the total length of exposure while the subjects are still at risk [before observing the first event or before completing the study for subjects without any event (censored)].

findings.why_wrong: Strand D treats Table 2's incidence rates as percentages and back-calculates approximately 132 and 129 participants. The footnote defines the denominators as time at risk, not participant counts. The resulting quantity is not a crude participant risk ratio.
findings.served_effect: Strand D presents unsupported participant denominators and a mislabeled crude risk ratio.
findings.proposed_fixture: Use the held CONFIRM-HF Table 2 headers, hospitalization row and footnote as input. Assert that incidence/100 patient-years cannot generate n1i/n2i or a PARTICIPANT_RISK row; specifically reject the displayed ~132/~129 denominators.

findings.title: EFFECT-HF hospitalization counts falsely marked absent

evidence.quote: 26 of them for worsening HF (13 in each group) in 17 patients (11 patients on FCM and 6 on usual care).

findings.why_wrong: The held full text explicitly supplies both recurrent hospitalization counts and patients hospitalized by arm. Lack of an extracted compatible effect does not establish source absence.
findings.served_effect: The unextracted-outcome audit conceals available hospitalization data and corroborates an incorrect absence verdict.
findings.proposed_fixture: Input the held hospitalization sentence under PMID 28701470. Assert that the hospitalization audit returns HELD_NOT_EXTRACTED or an extracted state, never NOT_IN_HELD_SOURCES, while preserving 13/13 events separately from 11/6 patients.

findings.title: CONFIRM-HF injection-site events falsely marked absent

evidence.quote: Of the patients reporting treatment-related adverse events with FCM, two patients experienced injection site discolouration, four patients reported feeling hot, and skin discolouration, urticaria, rash, and erythema were each reported by one patient.

findings.why_wrong: The full text reports two patients with injection-site discolouration, matching the configured injection-site outcome terms. Missing comparator counts would justify extraction debt, not outcome absence.
findings.served_effect: A reported administration-site harm is presented as unreported.
findings.proposed_fixture: Input this held sentence and the configured Injection-site reactions specification. Assert source_reported=true and an extracted or held-not-extracted state; do not infer a zero comparator count.

findings.title: Explicit zero hypersensitivity reports classified as unreported

evidence.quote: No hypersensitivity reactions to the drug occurred, and no cases of hypophosphatemia were reported.
No severe allergic reactions related to the study treatment were reported.

findings.why_wrong: EFFECT-HF explicitly reports no hypersensitivity reactions. CONFIRM-HF likewise reports no severe treatment-related allergic reactions and receives the same absence classification. These are reported zero-event statements, with their stated scope, rather than missing reporting.
findings.served_effect: The harm audit understates reporting and incorrectly certifies absence.
findings.proposed_fixture: Parameterize the two held sentences by PMID. Assert that each corresponding hypersensitivity row is source-reported and not NOT_IN_HELD_SOURCES or RETRIEVED_OUTCOME_NOT_REPORTED; retain the severity and treatment-related qualifiers.

findings.title: FAIR-HF2 rate ratio mislabeled HR in study_effect

evidence.quote: The second primary outcome (total heart failure hospitalizations) occurred 264 times in the ferric carboxymaltose group vs 320 times in the placebo group (rate ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.60-1.06]

findings.why_wrong: The source identifies 0.80 as a recurrent-event rate ratio. The nested study_effect copies the outcome-level HR label instead of preserving the trial's measure. The main incompatible pool is correctly suppressed, which limits but does not remove this field error.
findings.served_effect: Machine consumers receive an HR identity for an incidence rate ratio despite correct IRR labels elsewhere.
findings.proposed_fixture: Build a study_effect from the held FAIR-HF2 rate-ratio clause under an outcome preferring HR. Assert that its estimand remains IRR/INCIDENCE_RATE_RATIO and agrees with its effect_object.

findings.title: AFFIRM-AHF secondary report assigned a separate primary family

evidence.quote: We evaluated the impact of intravenous (IV) ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) vs. placebo on HRQoL for the AFFIRM-AHF population.
the latter was one of the predefined other secondary outcomes in the AFFIRM-AHF trial.

findings.why_wrong: PMID 34080008 analyzes a secondary outcome in the already represented AFFIRM-AHF population. It is not a separate primary trial.
findings.served_effect: The screening and absence ledgers count an additional primary report/family and expand their denominators. No duplicate pooled effect was established.
findings.proposed_fixture: Input the held AFFIRM-AHF primary and HRQoL reports. Assert that PMID 34080008 is secondary and shares the primary report's family, without adding an independent trial to outcome-reporting denominators.

findings.title: IRONMAN composite evidence adjudicates standalone hospitalization

evidence.quote: The primary outcome was recurrent hospital admissions for heart failure and cardiovascular death, assessed in all validly randomly assigned patients.

findings.why_wrong: This audit row uses the 336/411 primary-endpoint result to establish availability for standalone HF hospitalization. The held definition explicitly includes cardiovascular death. The separate composite strand correctly recognizes this distinction, but the audit does not.
findings.served_effect: The audit reports a standalone-outcome extraction obligation using evidence for a different outcome and marks the associated refusal REASON_FALSE_VALUE_HELD.
findings.proposed_fixture: Input IRONMAN's held primary definition and result clause with target components restricted to HF hospitalization. Assert that the composite result cannot establish HELD_NOT_EXTRACTED for the standalone target or invalidate a measure-mismatch refusal.

findings.title: Funder DOI parsed as an outcome fraction
findings.why_wrong: The value belongs to the funder's DOI metadata. It is not a numerator/denominator pair for hospitalization. The audit's fraction regex promotes an identifier fragment into an outcome-value field.
findings.served_effect: The PMID 34080008 hospitalization audit reports REASON_FALSE_VALUE_HELD with a funding identifier as numeric evidence.
findings.proposed_fixture: Pass the held funding XML and surrounding metadata through outcome-value detection. Assert that no clinical value is extracted from institution-id and that 13039/501100006484 is never emitted as value_text.

findings.title: CONFIRM-HF effect incorrectly described as absent from abstract

claim.quote: Abstract omits this isolated HF-hospitalisation effect (reports composite only), so it is a full-text recovery.

evidence.quote: Treatment with FCM was associated with a significant reduction in the risk of hospitalizations for worsening HF [hazard ratio (95% confidence interval): 0.39 (0.19-0.82), P = 0.009].

findings.why_wrong: The held abstract explicitly reports the isolated hospitalization HR and confidence interval.
findings.served_effect: The review misstates extraction provenance and the necessity of full-text recovery; the numerical effect itself is supported.
findings.proposed_fixture: Input the held PMID 25176939 abstract. Assert that the 0.39 HR is located in the abstract and prohibit the claims reports-composite-only and not-in-abstract for that effect.

findings.title: FCM-only comparator certified as matching the IV-iron class question

claim.quote: same-question comparator (matching intervention level and population)

evidence.quote: This meta-analysis seeks to provide updated insights into the effectiveness and safety of FCM compared to placebo/standard of care (SoC) among patients with HFrEF and ID/iron deficiency anemia (IDA).
intravenous iron, including ferric carboxymaltose, ferric derisomaltose, or iron sucrose.

findings.why_wrong: The comparator addresses ferric carboxymaltose specifically; the registered review addresses several IV-iron agents. It is a relevant narrower comparator, but intervention-level equivalence is not established.
findings.served_effect: The scope object marks intervention_level_match and scope_valid true and presents a narrower intervention question as identical.
findings.proposed_fixture: Compare the held FCM-only comparator scope with the protocol's three-agent intervention set. Assert a narrower-intervention relation rather than same-question intervention-level equivalence.
